events.title: Gas storage drains
events.desc: European gas inventories abnormally low at the start of winter.

events.title: Tensions escalate
events.desc: Russian troops mass at the Ukrainian border; gas prices begin to climb.

events.title: Invasion begins
events.desc: Russia invades Ukraine on Feb 24. Energy markets enter panic mode.

events.title: Nord Stream cuts
events.desc: Gazprom slashes Nord Stream flows; gas–power coupling spikes.

events.title: Peak prices
events.desc: Day-ahead electricity peaks above €700/MWh in many EU markets.

events.title: Nord Stream sabotage
events.desc: Pipeline ruptures end any return to pre-war Russian gas.

events.title: Easing
events.desc: Mild winter and demand cuts pull prices back below €200/MWh.

events.title: New normal
events.desc: Prices stabilise at a level still well above the 2018-2020 baseline.

events.title: Direct strikes
events.desc: Iran and Israel exchange direct strikes for the first time. Brent crude spikes.

events.title: Strait jitters
events.desc: Threats around the Strait of Hormuz lift LNG and oil benchmarks.

events.title: Sanctions tighten
events.desc: New US sanctions package targets Iranian crude exports.

events.title: Power-price echo
events.desc: European day-ahead prices nudge higher despite ample storage — a softer echo of 2022.

events.title: Stabilisation
events.desc: Markets price in a contained shock; prices remain near recent norms.
